title: The ghost lemma: a composition of maps that are zero on cohomology between stages of the generated subcategory vanishes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement is the ghost lemma: for an object of the n-th stage of the subcategory generated by the ring and a chain of n maps in the derived category, if every map in the chain is zero on cohomology then the composite vanishes (statement lines 20663-20677). The proof first settles the case of one stage by decomposing the object as a summand of shifts of the ring and using that maps out of a shift are computed by cohomology; the induction step then uses the distinguished triangle expressing a stage in terms of a one-stage object and the previous stage, factors the first map of the chain through the third term of the triangle using the one-stage case, and applies the induction hypothesis to the factored chain (proof lines 20679-20707). The factorization through the triangle is the heart of the induction. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed; the two references are carried as navigation stubs.
